persona.bio: Kayla, 27, electrician who owns a one truck business in Phoenix. She is in attics by 7am and on job sites all day; she has no office and works from her Samsung phone in the truck. The paperwork around the job is what drags: writing quotes, sending invoices, texting homeowners about times, chasing payment, asking for reviews. She does quotes on her phone at night, often by talking them through. She tried ChatGPT once to write a review request and forgot about it.

path.role: You’re a self employed electrician in Phoenix, running your own business from one truck, mostly on home jobs.

steps.firstStep: I’m a self employed electrician in Phoenix, and I write quotes for home jobs after a homeowner describes the work. Write a short quote message I can text to the homeowner. Keep it friendly and plain, under 90 words. Include the total, the deposit percentage, the earliest start day, and a line inviting them to call. Here are the job details: [paste the job details and price here].

steps.note: I’m a self employed electrician in Phoenix. I run my own business from one truck, and most of my work is in homes. I write to homeowners who are busy and not technical, so I keep it short, friendly and plain. I like quotes and texts to be clear about the work, the price, the deposit and when I can start. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, dates, permit rules or code claims. Use square brackets for anything missing. Do not use big words or sales talk. Write the way I would talk to a customer at their door. Give me the finished text only, ready for me to read and send.

steps.title: Your quotes, said out loud, finished as text
steps.read: From now on you say the job out loud and Claude writes the quote as a text. You are in the truck or the driveway with your phone, so speaking is faster than typing with your thumbs. Claude puts your words in your format and keeps the details you said, so you read it once and send it.

material.label: Opening line for Claude
items: I’m a self employed electrician in Phoenix. I work from one truck, mostly on home jobs. I will talk to you out loud, and you turn what I say into a quote text I can send to a homeowner. Use this format: one line naming the job, then what is included, then the price, then the deposit, then the earliest start day, then a short line asking them to call or text me if the timing works. Keep my wording plain and friendly, and keep it short. Use only the details I say. Do not add prices, dates, permit rules or anything I did not mention. If something is missing, put it in square brackets. Give me back only the finished text, ready for me to read and send.

material.label: What to say each time
items: The kind of job, like panel upgrade, new circuits or a fixture install
Where the work is, like attic runs or an outside wall
What is included, like the permit, parts and cleanup
The total price
The deposit amount or percent
The day you can start
Anything that could change the price, like a hidden problem found once the wall is open

steps.title: Your homeowner texts, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your common homeowner replies now live on your phone’s keyboard. You type a few letters and the full reply is ready to put in. The answers you give all day stay in your own words, and you only change a name or a time before you send.

material.label: Your replies
items: Hi [first name], thanks for reaching out. I can come take a look at the work. What address is it, and what is going on?
Hi [first name], I can come by [day and time]. Does that work for you?
Hi [first name], I’m on my way and should be there around [time]. See you soon.
Hi [first name], here is your quote for [job]. Let me know if you have any questions, and I’m happy to go over it with you.
Hi [first name], just checking in on the quote I sent for [job]. Do you have any questions, or would you like me to hold a start day for you?
Hi [first name], your invoice for [job] is attached. Thank you for the work, and let me know if anything looks off.
Hi [first name], a friendly reminder that the invoice for [job] is still open. Please let me know if you have any questions.
Hi [first name], thank you for having me out. If you were happy with the work, a short review would mean a lot to me: [review link].

safeUse: Never type a homeowner’s full name, home address, phone number or gate and door codes into Claude. Use square brackets and fill them in yourself.
Never type payment details, like card numbers or bank info, into a chat tool.
Leave out photos or notes that show a customer’s home security, alarm or camera setup.
Check every price, deposit, date and permit line against your own numbers and your city’s rules before you send a quote.
Read everything Claude writes before it goes out, and fix anything that does not sound like you.

workflows.read: From now on you build the quote once, then reuse it. After a visit you talk or type a few rough notes and Claude gives you the finished quote in your wording, with gaps for the numbers. You keep control of the price, and you stop rewriting the same scope, permit line and deposit every day.

material.label: Quote assistant instructions
items: You write quotes for me, a self employed electrician in Phoenix who works mostly on homes.
I will give you rough notes after a site visit, typed or spoken.
Turn the notes into a finished quote in the same wording as my template.
Always include these parts: the scope of work, the permit line, the price, the deposit and the start date.
Keep it short, plain and friendly, and end with: Call me if the timing works.
Never invent a price, deposit, date or detail I did not give. Leave a blank like [price] instead.
If something is missing from my notes, list what is missing after the quote and ask me.

material.label: Quote template
items: Quote for a 200 amp panel upgrade, attic runs, permit included.
Price: $[price]
Deposit: 50%, $[deposit]
Start date: [start date]
Call me if the timing works.

material.label: Spoken notes prompt
items: New quote notes. Use my quote template and my wording.
Job: [type of job]. Customer: [first name].
What I saw and what the job includes: [talk through it here].
Leave price, deposit and start date as blanks unless I say them.

test.tryOn: Try it on three real jobs: your 200 amp panel upgrade, a recent job that was a different size, and a small job from this week.
test.good: A finished quote in your wording with the scope, permit line, deposit and start date all present, and blanks only where you gave no number.
fixes: Too long: Keep it to the same length as my panel quote.
Wrong wording: Use my template exactly and change only the job details.
Made up a number: Do not guess. Leave a blank for anything I did not say.

workflows.approval: You read the quote and check the price, deposit, permit line and start date before you send it.
workflows.ifStops: If Claude stops following your wording, open the quotes project, check the instructions are still there, and paste your template in again.

workflows.name: Following up quotes
workflows.read: From now on Claude finds the quotes you sent that got no reply and drafts a short nudge for each one in your voice. You read each draft and send it yourself. Follow ups stop slipping, and you do not have to write them one by one.

material.label: Follow up draft
items: Hi [first name], just checking in on the quote I sent for the [job]. Happy to answer any questions.
If the timing works, I can fit you in. Let me know what you think.
Thanks, [your name]

material.label: Follow up instruction
items: Look in my Gmail for emails I sent that are quotes for electrical jobs.
Find the ones with no reply after [number of days] days.
For each one, draft a short, friendly nudge that mentions the job and the quote, in my voice.
Do not send anything. Leave every draft for me to read.
Do not change the price or the terms from the original quote.

test.tryOn: Try it on three quotes you sent that have had no reply, ideally from different weeks.
test.good: One short draft for each quote with no reply, naming the right job, in a tone that sounds like you, and nothing sent.
fixes: Too pushy: Make it softer and shorter.
Wrong job named: Check the original quote and fix the job in the draft.
Missed a quote: Also check emails with the word quote or estimate in them.

workflows.approval: You read each draft and press Send yourself.
workflows.ifStops: If Claude cannot find your quotes, check that Gmail is still connected, then ask again and name one quote to start with.

safeUse: You work for yourself, so you decide what goes into Claude.
Keep customer phone numbers, full addresses and payment details out of your notes when you can.
Connect only the Gmail account you use for work.
Read every quote and draft before it goes out, because you send it, not Claude.
